title: Completion commutes with the finite polynomial quotient used in the degree-p step
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring (a ring with exactly one maximal ideal, here $\mathfrak m$) and $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$ its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with $\iota:R\to R^\wedge$. Let $p\geq1$ be an integer, $f\in R$, and $C=R[z]/(z^p-f)$, the quotient of the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] by the ideal generated by $z^p-f$, with $\varphi:R\to C$. Assume $C$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, and let $C^\wedge=\varprojlim_nC/\mathfrak n^n$ be its $\mathfrak n$-adic completion, with $\iota_C:C\to C^\wedge$. Then there is an isomorphism of rings $\theta:R^\wedge[z]/(z^p-\iota(f))\xrightarrow{\sim}C^\wedge$ compatible with the maps from $R[z]$ to both sides (on the left $R[z]\to R^\wedge[z]\to R^\wedge[z]/(z^p-\iota(f))$, applying $\iota$ to the coefficients and $z\mapsto z$; on the right $R[z]\to C\xrightarrow{\iota_C}C^\wedge$). Moreover $R^\wedge\otimes_RC\to C^\wedge$, $a\otimes c\mapsto a\cdot\iota_C(c)$, is an isomorphism of $C$-algebras and of $R^\wedge$-algebras, where $R^\wedge=\varprojlim R/\mathfrak m^n$ acts on $C^\wedge$ through the maps $R/\mathfrak m^n\to C/\mathfrak n^n$ induced by $\varphi$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, degree-p step: 'the completion of C = B[z]/(z^p-f) equals B_r^\wedge[z]/(z^p-f)'; the finite-quotient completion argument uses Algebra Lemma Tag 00MA and completion-finite-extension Tag 07N9

proof.text: ($C$ is finite and integral over $R$.) The polynomial $z^p-f\in R[z]$ is monic of degree $p\ge1$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] $C=R[z]/(z^p-f)$ is a free $R$-module with basis the classes of $1,z,\dots,z^{p-1}$; in particular $C$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] $C$ is integral over $R$ (via $\varphi$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring, line 12306), proof: 'the completion of C = B[z]/(z^p-f) equals B_r^\wedge[z]/(z^p-f)' (stated without argument)

proof.text: ($\mathfrak n$ is the only prime of $C$ over $\mathfrak m$.) Since $\varphi$ is integral (step 1) and $\mathfrak n$ is maximal, $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ is a maximal ideal of $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal]; $R$ being local, $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m$. Conversely let $\mathfrak q\subset C$ be a prime with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak m$. Since $\mathfrak m$ is maximal and $\varphi$ is integral, $\mathfrak q$ is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], so $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak n$, $C$ having only one maximal ideal. Hence the primes of $C$ lying over $\mathfrak m$ are exactly $\mathfrak q_1=\mathfrak n$ (one prime, $m=1$ in the notation of 07N9).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension), applied with p = m

proof.text: (Localizing a local ring at its maximal ideal changes nothing.) In the local ring $R$ every element $t\notin\mathfrak m$ is a unit (otherwise $tR$ is a proper ideal, contained in a maximal ideal, which can only be $\mathfrak m$). So by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-units-or-zero] (2), applied to the localization $R\to R_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] at $T=R\setminus\mathfrak m$, the map $R\to R_{\mathfrak m}$, $r\mapsto r/1$, is an isomorphism of rings; it carries $\mathfrak m^n$ onto $\mathfrak m^nR_{\mathfrak m}$, hence induces isomorphisms $R/\mathfrak m^n\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak m^nR_{\mathfrak m}$ commuting with the reductions $n+1\to n$, and so an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $R^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak m^nR_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] (componentwise). In the same way, $C$ being local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, $C\to C_{\mathfrak n}$ is an isomorphism carrying $\mathfrak n^n$ onto $\mathfrak n^nC_{\mathfrak n}$, and induces an isomorphism of $C$-algebras $C^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_{\mathfrak n})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nC_{\mathfrak n}/\mathfrak n^nC_{\mathfrak n}$. Under these identifications the local map $R_{\mathfrak m}\to C_{\mathfrak n}$, $r/t\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$, is $\varphi$ (both composites $R\to C_{\mathfrak n}$ equal $r\mapsto\varphi(r)/1$), so the map $(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge\to(C_{\mathfrak n})^\wedge$ it induces becomes the map $R^\wedge\to C^\wedge$ induced by $R/\mathfrak m^n\to C/\mathfrak n^n$ (well defined as $\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$ by step 2).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension), applied with p = m

proof.text: (The tensor product is the completion.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] to the Noetherian ring $R$, the ring map $\varphi:R\to C$ making $C$ a finitely generated $R$-module (step 1) and the prime $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$ (maximal, hence prime); by step 2 the primes of $C$ over $\mathfrak m$ are just $\mathfrak q_1=\mathfrak n$. It gives an isomorphism of $C$-algebras $(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge\otimes_RC\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_{\mathfrak n})^\wedge$, compatible with the $(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge$-algebra structures, $(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge$ acting on the right through the map induced by $R_{\mathfrak m}\to C_{\mathfrak n}$. Composing with the isomorphisms of step 3 (and $R^\wedge\otimes_RC\cong(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge\otimes_RC$, the tensor product of the $R$-algebra isomorphism of step 3 with the identity of $C$) gives an isomorphism $\gamma:R^\wedge\otimes_RC\xrightarrow{\sim}C^\wedge$ of $C$-algebras and of $R^\wedge$-algebras ($R^\wedge$ acting on $C^\wedge$ through $R/\mathfrak m^n\to C/\mathfrak n^n$). Being $C$-linear and $R^\wedge$-linear with $\gamma(1\otimes1)=1$, it is $\gamma(a\otimes c)=a\cdot\iota_C(c)$. This is the second assertion. (The $\mathfrak n$-adic versus $\mathfrak m$-adic topology on $C$ is handled inside the cited lemma, its step 4.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension), statement, with p = m and one prime n over it; its last step is Lemma Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor)

proof.text: (Base change of the presentation.) The quotient map $\pi:R[z]\to C$ is a presentation of $C$ over $R$ with one variable and one relation $z^p-f$ (the polynomial ring in one variable [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is the case $J=\{1\}$ of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]). By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] with $R'=R^\wedge$, the $R^\wedge$-algebra map $\pi':R^\wedge[z]\to C\otimes_RR^\wedge$, $z\mapsto\bar z\otimes1$, is surjective with kernel generated by $z^p-\iota(f)$ (the image of $z^p-f$ under $\iota$ on coefficients). Hence, composing with the swap $C\otimes_RR^\wedge\cong R^\wedge\otimes_RC$, we get an isomorphism of $R^\wedge$-algebras $\delta:R^\wedge[z]/(z^p-\iota(f))\xrightarrow{\sim}R^\wedge\otimes_RC$ with $\delta(\bar z)=1\otimes\bar z$. Put $\theta=\gamma\circ\delta$ (step 4), a ring isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring, line 12306), proof: 'the completion of C = B[z]/(z^p-f) equals B_r^\wedge[z]/(z^p-f)' (stated without argument)

proof.text: (Compatibility with the maps from $R[z]$.) Let $\alpha:R[z]\to R^\wedge[z]/(z^p-\iota(f))$ and $\beta=\iota_C\circ\pi:R[z]\to C^\wedge$ be the two maps of the statement. Both $\theta\circ\alpha$ and $\beta$ are $R$-algebra maps ($R$ acting on $C^\wedge$ through $\iota_C\circ\varphi$, which equals the action through $\iota$ and the $R^\wedge$-structure, both being $r\mapsto(\varphi(r)\bmod\mathfrak n^n)_n$), since $\theta$ is $R^\wedge$-linear. On $z$: $\theta(\alpha(z))=\gamma(\delta(\bar z))=\gamma(1\otimes\bar z)=\iota_C(\bar z)=\beta(z)$ by steps 4 and 5. Two $R$-algebra maps out of $R[z]$ that agree on $z$ are equal [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so $\theta\circ\alpha=\beta$. This is the first assertion.

lean.statement: theorem completion_finite_quotient (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) (f : R) [IsLocalRing (AdjoinRoot (X ^ p - C f))] : let S := AdjoinRoot (X ^ p - C f) let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R let n := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S let Rhat := AdicCompletion m R let Shat := AdicCompletion n S let ι := algebraMap R Rhat let ιS := algebraMap S Shat let φ := algebraMap R S ∃ g : Rhat →+* Shat, (∀ (a : Rhat) (k : ℕ) (r : R), evalₐ m k a = Ideal.Quotient.mk (m ^ k) r → evalₐ n k (g a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (n ^ k) (φ r)) ∧ (∃ θ : AdjoinRoot (X ^ p - C (ι f)) ≃+* Shat, ∀ q : R[X], θ (AdjoinRoot.mk _ (Polynomial.map ι q)) = ιS (AdjoinRoot.mk _ q)) ∧ (∃ γ : (Rhat ⊗[R] S) ≃+* Shat, ∀ (a : Rhat) (c : S), γ (a ⊗ₜ[R] c) = g a * ιS c)

reviewed_lean.note: Noetherian local (R,m) as IsNoetherianRing+IsLocalRing/maximalIdeal; p>=1 as ℕ with 1≤p; C=AdjoinRoot(X^p-C f) (literally R[X]/span) with C local as instance, n its maximalIdeal; completions AdicCompletion m R / n S with algebraMap; R^-action g pinned levelwise via evalₐ (unique, = induced R/m^k→C/n^k); θ ring iso compatible with all of R[z]; γ ring iso with a⊗c↦g a*ιS c (both algebra compatibilities); ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian is m-adic linear only → existing:false right
